lore: Thieves have always had quick hands. Lately they've had quicker feet: a Sneak Attack now often lands before the beast can answer, and the forest seems to drop its valuables in a thief's path a little more often than anyone else's.
plain: Thieves: Sneak Attack dodges the counterattack half the time, and thieves find loot more often (5% vs 3%).

lore: The town crier has been asked, politely, to stop following you into your place of work. He took it well. The news will keep until you come through the gate.
plain: No more realm news or mail notes at the start of your Claude Code sessions. Nothing shows until you enter; the ⚔ and ✉ in the status line still do.

lore: There's music in the tavern now, and not always the same music. Some nights it's a cheerful piper, some nights an old man with a ballad that never ends, a minstrel singing about himself, or a woman in the corner who barely speaks. Ask nicely. A good song can do strange things for you.
plain: A bard plays the (T)avern each day — Fennick Reed, Dunstan the Unfinished, Corwin Lark or Wren. (L)isten once a day for a song and, sometimes, a small gift.

lore: You step outside and the sky looks familiar. It ought to: it's the same one over your own roof, more or less. When it rains where you are, it rains in the forest too.
plain: The realm's weather follows your real weather, from your rough location (never stored). Ask to turn it off any time.

lore: There are new faces in town. A monk is up before the roosters, the stable lad has found a sword, a fortune teller has hung a curtain in the back of the tavern, and someone called Sir Pomfrey would like you to notice his armor.
plain: Four new townsfolk: Brother Ansel, Pip, Madam Orsolya and Sir Pomfrey. They show up in (R)ankings and the tavern.

lore: There's a new page nailed to the inside of your door, in a hand you don't recognize. It seems to know what's changed in the realm since you last slept, and it means to tell you.
plain: After an update, the game tells you what's new, once.

lore: Your name is cut a little deeper into the inn's sign now, with a small mark beneath it. When the realm shifts, you'll feel it before anyone tells you.
plain: The title screen shows your version, and the game tells you when an update is out.

lore: A crossed pair of swords has been scratched into the corner of your vision. It glints whenever something happens in the realm that you haven't heard about yet.
plain: ⚔ N in your Claude Code status line for news you haven't read. (N)ews clears it.

lore: The old sign over the gate has come down in the night. The new one is carved in heavier wood: Dragon's Door.
plain: Dragonmoor is now Dragon's Door. The command is /dragons-door:enter.

lore: Someone has painted the dragon over the gate, wings and all. You'll see it each time you come through.
plain: A title screen when you enter.

lore: A small envelope seems to hang at the edge of your sight whenever a letter is waiting, even when you're busy with other work.
plain: ✉ N in your Claude Code status line. Set it up with /dragons-door:statusline.

lore: A pigeon loft has gone up behind the inn. Letters come and go now, and the townsfolk keep their own hours — some at dawn, some long after dark.
plain: (M)ail to send and read letters. Townsfolk play at different times through the day.

lore: You wake and notice something new in your room. A brown leather satchel sits in the corner, its strap worn soft. Now and then, a beast in the forest drops something worth keeping.
plain: Rare loot drops, and a bag to carry them in. (G)ear to look inside; bigger bags at the shop. Die, and you lose one thing from it.
